definitions.explanation: A history compiled privately rather than by the state, often preserving anecdotes and folk accounts left out of official records. Contrasted with {正史|せいし}, the authorized dynastic history.

examples.japanese: {野史|やし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{記|しる}される→記す：14238_shirusu⟧。
examples.english: It is recorded in unofficial histories.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正史|せいし}→正史：29614_seishi⟧にない⟦{逸話|いつわ}→逸話：14322_itsuwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{野史|やし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{残|のこ}る→残る：01187_nokoru⟧。
examples.english: Anecdotes absent from the official history survive in unofficial histories.

examples.japanese: ⟦{当時|とうじ}→当時：01615_touji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{庶民|しょみん}→庶民：12427_shomin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{暮|く}らし→暮らし：02670_kurashi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{野史|やし}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{知|し}る→知る：00458_shiru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: The daily life of common people of the time can be learned from unofficial histories.

notes:
Composed of {野|や} (unofficial, rustic) + ⟦{史|し}→〜史：28471_shi⟧ (history). A somewhat literary term.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{正史|せいし}→正史：29614_seishi⟧: official history — state-compiled and authoritative, the direct antonym
- {外史|がいし}: unofficial history — a close synonym, common in the titles of historical works
